# Plain C# codebases in ordinary hand-written style

- **Status:** Done 2026-10-28 (commit 6152609, authored by Codex; the generated plain C# codebases are ordinary hand-written style with no Phrase vocabulary; Decider D87 passed; the condition of D85 is met)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; generator change)
- **Milestone:** Codebase size: does Phrase's cost fall and its edge widen as the codebase grows?
- **Source:** Decider D85 (2026-10-27), review of card 119: the generated plain C# codebase reuses emitter-style files (Phrases.cs, PhraseRuntime.cs, a PhraseAttribute and a PhraseFailure type), so it is not a fair ordinary-C# baseline for a size experiment.
- **Depends on:** 119
- **Story:** As Riley, I want the generated plain C# codebases written the way a developer would write them, with no Phrase names, attributes or runtime types, so that the size experiment compares Phrase with ordinary C#.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given sizes 1, 10 and 50, When the generator writes the plain C# codebase, Then no file, type, attribute or comment contains the words Phrase or phrase, it uses ordinary FastEndpoints endpoints, request and response records, a plain exception or result type for declared failures, and ordinary service classes for shared rules (a test searches every generated file)
  2. Given the plain C# codebase, When it is built and its xUnit tests run, Then it builds without warnings and passes the same shared outcome cases as before (the byte-identical outcomes check from card 119 stays green)
  3. Given the modify and fix tasks, When they are regenerated, Then each still needs context from another file and its starting code is the same size class as the Phrase version's (a test names the dependency and compares the size classes)
